title: The Book of Ruth Timeline
sub: Your People Will Be My People · Redemption at the City Gate
desc: A Moabite widow's vow of loyalty to her mother-in-law leads her into the field of a kinsman-redeemer named Boaz, ending in a marriage whose great-grandson would become King David.

eras.label: Era One · Ruth 1
eras.name: Famine, Loss, and a Vow of Loyalty
eras.dates: A family flees famine to Moab and loses everything, until one widowed daughter-in-law refuses to let another widow return home alone

events.title: Famine Drives a Family to Moab: Three Widows Left Behind
events.detail: Famine in Bethlehem sends Elimelech's family to Moab, where he and both his sons die, leaving Naomi and her two Moabite daughters-in-law, Orpah and Ruth, as three widows with no male protector.

verses.text: “Then Naomi's two sons, Mahlon and Kilion, also died. So the woman was left all alone—bereaved of her two children as well as her husband!”

events.title: Your People Will Be My People, Your God My God
events.detail: Naomi urges both daughters-in-law to return to their own families, and Orpah does; Ruth instead clings to Naomi with one of Scripture's most quoted vows of loyalty, and the two women return together to a bitter, empty homecoming in Bethlehem.

verses.text: “Wherever you go, I will go. Wherever you live, I will live. Your people will become my people, and your God [Elohim] will become my God [Elohim].”
“Call me ‘Mara’ because the Almighty [Shaddai] has treated me very harshly… the LORD [Yahweh] has caused me to return empty-handed.”

eras.label: Era Two · Ruth 2
eras.name: Ruth Gleans in the Field of Boaz
eras.dates: A chance arrival in a stranger's field turns out to be nothing of the kind, introducing the man who will become the story's redeemer

events.title: She Just Happened to End Up in the Field of Boaz
events.detail: Ruth's search for grain to glean leads her, seemingly by chance, into the field of Boaz, a wealthy relative of Naomi's late husband, who notices her loyalty to Naomi and offers her protection and provision beyond what custom required.

verses.text: “May your acts of kindness be repaid fully by the LORD [Yahweh] the God [Elohim] of Israel, from whom you have sought protection.”

events.title: Naomi Recognizes a Guardian-Redeemer
events.detail: Boaz quietly instructs his workers to leave extra grain for Ruth to find, and when she brings home an unusually large harvest, Naomi recognizes Boaz's name and identifies him as one of the family's potential guardian-redeemers.

verses.text: “May he be rewarded by the LORD [Yahweh] because he has shown loyalty to the living on behalf of the dead!… This man is a close relative of ours; he is our guardian.”

eras.label: Era Three · Ruth 3
eras.name: The Threshing Floor — a Bold Request at Midnight
eras.dates: Naomi orchestrates a daring nighttime plan that puts the question of redemption directly to Boaz himself

events.title: Spread Your Covering Over Your Servant, for You Are a Redeemer
events.detail: Naomi sends Ruth to the threshing floor at night to formally request that Boaz act as guardian-redeemer; Boaz agrees in principle but reveals a closer relative has first right of refusal, promising to resolve it the very next day.

verses.text: “I am Ruth, your servant. Spread your covering over your servant, for you are a guardian of the family interests.”

eras.label: Era Four · Ruth 4
eras.name: Redemption at the City Gate — the Great-Grandfather of David
eras.dates: A legal transaction at the town gate resolves the story, ending in a genealogy that quietly reveals the book's largest stakes

events.title: The Nearer Redeemer Declines: Boaz Acquires Ruth as His Wife
events.detail: At the city gate, the closer relative declines to redeem the land once he learns it requires marrying Ruth, formally transferring his right to Boaz through the sandal-removal custom, witnessed publicly by the town's elders.

verses.text: “I have also acquired Ruth the Moabite, the wife of Mahlon, as my wife to raise up a descendant who will inherit his property.”

events.title: Obed, the Father of Jesse, the Father of David
events.detail: Boaz and Ruth marry and have a son, Obed, whom the village women celebrate as a guardian-redeemer given to Naomi in her old age, and the closing genealogy quietly reveals Obed as the grandfather of King David himself.

verses.text: “May the LORD [Yahweh] be praised because he has not left you without a guardian today! May he become famous in Israel!”
“They named him Obed. Now he became the father of Jesse—David's father.”
